items.title: Listener Emails on Meta Glasses, Luna AI, Runa TTS and Braille Pricing
items.description: Should blind and low vision users install iOS 27 right away? Steven Scott and Shaun Preece explain why VoiceOver users might wait a month. Then they open the inbox for listener emails on Meta glasses problems, the best smart glasses for reading, Luna AI, Siri dictation and the high cost of Braille displays.

items.title: Is AI Really That Dangerous? Will Guyatt Joins, Plus First Thoughts on Siri AI
items.description: Is the AI industry sounding a real alarm, or is it about money? Tech journalist Will Guyatt joins Steven Scott and Shaun Preece to make sense of the AI pause warnings. Then it's a first look at Siri AI in the iOS 27 beta and a candid chat about Windows, the Mac and screen readers.

items.title: Mainstream: Marc Aflalo’s Take On Apple’s ‘Surprise And Shine’ Event
items.description: Apple's Surprise and Shine event brought the foldable iPhone Duo, AirPods 5 and a quiet RAM boost for Apple Watch Ultra 4. Steven Scott and Marc Aflalo of YourTechReport pick out what matters, what could have been a press release, and whether the Duo can replace an iPad for someone who travels a lot.

items.title: Weekend Classic: Honda Cynic
items.description: Honda Scenic Audio set out to describe the view from a car window for blind and visually impaired passengers, using computer vision and generative AI. Steven Scott and Shaun Preece revisit their 2024 conversation about the app, built with Perkins School for the Blind, and ask whether poetic AI scenery description is something blind people actually want.

items.title: Audio Description For Sighted People, Clipman Updates, and the AI Extinction Story
items.description: Audio description was built for blind and partially sighted viewers. RNIB brought broadcasters to London to ask whether sighted audiences want it too, and what that would change for the rest of us. Steven Scott reports back from the Audio Is King event, before the show turns to Clipman, an Audacity 4 warning, and the Anthropic resignation that put AI extinction talk on every front page.

items.description: Introducing Double Tap Live. A 24/7 streaming audio channel dedicated to accessibility, assistive technology and disability inclusion. Always on. Launching Wednesday, September 30 at 1pm Eastern.
